subject: science
passage: Like most cephalopods, the common octopus has eyes containing only one type of light-sensitive pigment, an arrangement that in other animals goes along with an inability to tell colors apart. Laboratory tests have generally confirmed this expectation: octopuses trained to choose between objects that differ in color but not in brightness perform no better than chance. ______ octopuses match the colors of the reefs and seaweeds around them with striking accuracy, shifting the hue of their skin within a fraction of a second, an ability whose basis researchers are still working to explain.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first two sentences build an expectation that octopuses cannot distinguish colors, and lab tests support it. The last sentence reports something that seems to conflict with that expectation: octopuses still match colors accurately. The transition must show that this ability exists in spite of what came before, while the earlier facts remain true.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Instead" signals that one thing replaces another, but the color matching does not replace the single pigment or the test results; all of these facts stand together. This is the closest near miss because it also sounds like a contrast.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Therefore" would make accurate color matching a result of having only one pigment, which reverses the logic: one pigment would lead us to expect poor color matching.
explanation.C: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that octopuses match colors well despite the evidence that they cannot tell colors apart.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a point that resembles the previous one, but the color matching conflicts with the test results rather than resembling them.
